source.stem: An ideal converging lens of focal length 15 cm lies between a fixed object and a screen 80 cm apart. Can it be placed at two distinct positions producing a sharp image? Find those distances and explain the physical domain.
source.decisive_work: Establish when there are two distinct physical conjugate positions instead of blindly solving a quadratic.

shortest_valid_route: Set p+q=D under positive real-screen distances
Combine pq=fD and the two lens positions to derive f=(D²−d²)/(4D)
Recover the two allowed lens positions and verify the product and sum
Apply discriminant test to the changed track, including the double-root case
task.protected_decisive_work: Infer f from observed conjugate separation, then test a changed track against the discriminant boundary.
task.model_conditions: Ideal thin converging lens with f>0, paraxial rays, fixed real object and screen distance D, real sharp image at the screen, lens located between object and screen.

concept_model_selection.evidence: Select the two-conjugate thin-lens model under fixed screen geometry

representation_translation.evidence: Translate lens-position separation to root sum and difference

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Invert two measurements and reject a competing model at the boundary

algebra_computational_load.evidence: One quadratic/product calculation after the physical representation

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: Distinguish two distinct roots from one double root at D=4f
